done_when: The worker brief lets a worker change a file outside its Scope that the change needs, naming each such file and why in its handoff, and the review reports only outside-Scope files the work doesn't need; workers still stop for a one-way step, a security question, a new moving part or contradicting Done-when items. The brief and the review ask for an end-to-end test only for items that change runtime behaviour; settings, docs, deletions and test-only items are proven by the check the item names. The brief tells workers to name new test files after the behaviour they prove, never after the fix's slug.

findings.body: The new instruction asks the reviewer to report outside-Scope files the work does not need, but the list supplied to the reviewer still omits every changed existing test outside Scope. In `src/forge/review.py:214-215`, the `p in existing_tests and _test_file(p)` filter excludes those files without checking whether the work needed them. The existing test at `tests/test_fix_workers_stop_to_ask_before_updating_an_e.py:81-84` explicitly preserves that exclusion. An unrelated change to an existing test can therefore be absent from the review’s outside-Scope list. Include those files so the reviewer can assess necessity and the handoff reason.
findings.title: Not done: Review must assess all files outside Scope

findings.body: The worker brief embeds `src/forge/standards.md` through `src/forge/worker.py:364-372`. Immediately after the changed conditional rule, `src/forge/standards.md:236-237` still says every user-facing item gets a Playwright test and every item without UI gets an HTTP test. The brief also points workers to `src/forge/templates/conventions/testing.md:25-27`, which still requires an end-to-end test for every Done-when item. These unconditional rules conflict with the new instruction that settings, docs, deletions and test-only items use their named check, so the brief can still send workers to build unnecessary end-to-end tests.
findings.title: Not done: Limit all worker end-to-end test rules to runtime changes

why: Workers stop and ask before every file outside their Scope, even a caller or type file the change plainly needs, and the brief demands an end-to-end test for every item even for docs, settings, deletions and test-only changes, so workers and reviews waste rounds
